                   Provincial Government (Preparatory Arrangements) Act
1974

                         SUSPENSION ORDER
  I JOHN GUISE, G.C.M.G., Governor-General, by virtue of the powers
conferred by Sections 9A and 9D of the
    Provincial Government (Preparatory Arrangements) Act 1974, and
all other powers me enabling, acting with,
  and in accordance with, the advice of the National Executive
Council, being of the opinion that it is in the
  national interest to do so, hereby—
      (a) order that all the powers and functions of the Provincial
Government of Bougainville be suspended;
        and
      (b) appoint the persons specified in Column 1 of the Schedule
to be the Bougainville Provincial Trust;
        and
      (c) appoint each person specified in Column 2 of the Schedule
opposite the name of a person specified
        in Column 1 to be the deputy of that person.

      (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation, the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with

          a crop/crops or pasture species of economic value, which
shall be harvested regularly in accordance with sound com-

            mercial practice:


             One half in the first period of 5 years of the term;

           Four-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the term;
and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the land so

                suitable shall be kept so planted.


      (b) Provided always that if at the end of the first two (2)
years of the term, the lessee has not made such progress

with the land preparation and plantings as to suggest that
he will fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister, for

          Lands after considering any reply from the lessee to a
demand to show cause why he (the Minister) should not so do

          may, by notice in the Gazette and in accordance with the
Land Act 1962, as amended to date, forfeit the Lease.


      (c) The lessee or his agent shall take up residency or
occupancy of the block within six months of date of grant.


      (d) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great

          cattle per 3 ha. within 1 year from the date of grant, and
1 head of great cattle per 2 hectares within 4 years from

          the date of grant and shall be kept stocked to that
minimum for the remainder of the term.


          That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall within 1 year from the date of grant be fenced

          externally with a barbed wire fence of not less than four
strands having posts not more than 4.5 metres (15 feet)

          apart and strainer posts at least every 100 metres (5
chains) the said fence to be kept well strained and in stock-proof

          condition.


      (f) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be subdivided by fences into at least three paddocks,

          none of which shall exceed one half of the area within 2
years from the date of grant.


      (g) Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date

          of grant.


      (h) Conditions of improvements may at the discretion of the
Minister for Lands upon the recommendation of the

Land Board be modified in accordance with the detailed development

proposals of the applicant submitted in evidence to the

Land Board.


    Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or
posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani, Papua

New Guinea before 3 p.m., Wednesday, 10th December, 1975. All
applications must be accompanied by the prescribed fee of

K2.00 for each lease required. Applications not conforming to these
requirements will be rejected as informal.


14th October, 1975.

display a ticket, label, placard. or notice -attached- to or,

shall within two years of date of grant, be fenced externally

           except in such parts of the boundaries as the presence of
natural features make this unnecessary, with a barbed wire fence

           of not less than four strands the topmost of which shall
be suspended not less than 1.1 metres above the ground and

           having posts not more than 4.5 metres apart, and strainer
posts at least every, 100 metres. The said fence to be kept

well strained, and in a stock-proof condition,

           of the total grazed area of the base, within 4 years from

Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date

           of grant and maintained in serviceable condition for the
duration of the lease.

stocked as the following rate—

           and from the expiration of these periods the respective

THE Papua New Guinea National Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrangements
  set out below:
Public Service Gazette
   Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New
Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.
General Gazette
  • General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory
rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weekly at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.
Special Gazette
   Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the
Government Printing Office at 10 toea and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.
Subscriptions
   Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:
   Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15.00 per annum; K7.50
per half year; K3.75 per quarter;
   Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9.00 per half
year; K4.50 per quarter;
   Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half
year; K13.75 per quarter.
Notices
   "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government

Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-
fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and
Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing
date.
   All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.
The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in f articular and
proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,
